Very unique take on the survival game genre, but really overshadowed by tedious and boring game mechanics. We found the game to be more fun when abusing its glitches and bugs.

Everything I will be describing came from a multiplayer session with my friend. I don't have much experience regarding singleplayer.

The first few hours of raft are extremely tedious. Sometimes a run can end because the game decides, that no resources will drift your way when you badly need them. 

The normal loot collection loop is insanely tedious and boring. The shark non-stop being on your ass doesn't make it more fun. The game expects you to collect an absolutely ridiculous amount of wood, plastic and metal. Planting trees on your raft barely speeds it up and collecting them by hand nets barely anything to work with. Plastic only drifts into your raft and metal, scrap etc come from gathering next to islands. Don't even get me started on the processing times for some of the materials via the Smelter. Many of the games mechanics artificially inflate your game time for no real reason.

Weapon durability being low and no repair station make this even worse, since you have to always craft a completely fresh set of tools if they break.

Gathering animals is insanely tedious. We beat the entire story without finding a single llama, because they just didn't spawn. Meanwhile, we had like 6 chickens and a goat.

Equipment breaks really quick, to the point where it might not even be worth crafting. I expect the same with armor (we never crafted it). The bow has a learning curve behind it, but even after using it for 20 hours it still felt bad, especially against any flying enemy.

To circumvent the absolutely tedious general gameplay loop, we starting dupping items via an exploit with saving and loading a backup. Problem is, that even with the huge amounts of resources, we didn't have enough for what we wanted to do/basic tools + basic infrastructure. I have no idea how the game expects you to collect so much wood, plastic, metal, scrap and titanium, when some recipes already take a large amount of it and that's just to craft said thing once.

The game's story consists of random scattered notes and a few locations. It's just kinda there and not really super interesting. You could probably "beat" the game in less than 5 hours if you really tried. The story mostly serves to give you tools to survive better and move to the next story location. Some of the puzzles were fun / interesting, but a lot of the time it's very straightforward. Some where just "go here, find this, then come back". Those were not very fun.

There are definitely a lot of bugs in multiplayer at least. A big one we encountered was, that the advanced controls caused the advanced anchor to be in a superposition. It was lowered for me, but not for the other player, causing the raft to glitch out. Some other meaningful ones I can mention are: completely negating fall damage, climbing walls vertically etc.

Overall, the game expects you to put in a ridiculous amount of time gathering simple resources and doing the same thing over and over again (gathering treasure for example). Don't even get me started on the achievement list. It has to be one of the worst ones I've ever seen in a video game, nothing but do this x50 times for no real reason. No fun. The idea behind the game is good, but the execution of game mechanics really drags down the entire experience. I'm sure some people could enjoy a really slow paced survival game that takes real hours and that offers doing stuff over and over again. But I don't think tedious game mechanics and wasting your time for no reason is fun or engaging.

If you were looking for a raft-building survival crafting game that takes place on the water, this is the one to go to!

I think your alternatives are Tidewrack (not as well rated) or Stranded Deep (not raft-focused). It's fun, but there are some frustrations. Quite a number of tools are a mystery to unlock and use. In particular, I spent about 50 hours of the game just doing base building -- having fun, mind you -- before I realized I hadn't "researched" copper, which ludicrously unlocks circuit boards, then antennas, then radar and ... GPS mapping systems??? Until then you'll simply hit the same islands over and over and will never locate any of the storyline. And the storyline? Well it's fine. It's uneven. The story is about people who came before you, what happened to the world such that it's all so wet all over, and the struggles they dealt with. 

A lot of the tech tree is silly, just go in knowing that and you'll be fine. This is not ultrarealism. There is a meager list of nice-to-have items that make raft travel better but most are unlocked well into the story. For me I was already done at that point having put in nearly 100 hours. Some of that time was spent getting back up to speed: every time you die, you lose 2/3rds of your stuff. If you're playing multiplayer, apparently, you can be resuscitated by a friend, and keep your stuff, but if you're single player shame on you. There's no body you can fetch, you just lose most of your stuff, so make sure to leave unnecessary crap in a locker before you do a dangerous thing. 

Also quick tip don't do any renovating near your lockers or chests, because you may accidentally trigger a timespace conniption whereby all your contents try to exist in the same space at the same time and you lose almost everything. That was fun. I didn't throw anything across the room at all, I was very poised.

You use a  scrap hook to pick up scrap metal off the ocean floor, but the shovel won't work. You use a machete to strike a shark or warthog, but not an axe. You melt iron ore into metal bars which is used to build most heavy things, but you get nails from scrap which can't be likewise melted down. You can't use a shovel to row your raft, because that needs a paddle, and a paddle requires plastic. Lots of little things like that.

Still, you get to explore different islands, fight off sharks, build fairly big raft mobile homes if you want to invest the time, craft things into other things, and get an under-playtested but worthwhile back story. I had fun.

A brilliant, oceanic survival sandbox that transforms a stranded-at-sea nightmare into a deeply addictive and cozy crafting experience. You start on a tiny 2x2 wooden square armed only with a plastic hook, and your goal is to pull trash from the ocean to build a massive, floating fortress. The progression loop is incredibly rewarding as you transition from basic survival to automation and island exploration, though the repetitive early-game gathering and the relentless, annoying shark can test your patience.

PROS:
• Incredibly satisfying base-building that lets you build massive, fully customized rafts.
• Addictive progression loop from basic plastic-hooking to high-tech automation.
• Smooth and deeply engaging co-op experience—perfect to play with friends.
• Exploring unique, story-driven islands adds a refreshing break from drifting.

CONS:
• Early-game resource gathering can feel highly repetitive and slow.
• The shark mechanic is less scary and more of a constant, annoying chore.
